answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked until its actions are audited; if independent reviewers confirm coordinated fake identities, the bond is slashed and the accounts lose access to future work. A willow-linked reputation graph can flag accounts funded by the same source, while an ember-sized trial job limits losses before trust grows. The mirror is the cost: an attacker must lock real capital for every identity and risks losing it, so creating sybils is no longer free. This does not prove identities are unique, but makes large attacks expensive and detectable.
